rows.observableExpectedBehavior: A newly selected view or stage does not inherit an unrelated prior view's scroll offset; the actual next action is visible after Save and Workflow navigation. Restoration still applies the saved view position. Forward auto-focus within the destination view moves downward, not toward an offscreen earlier element.
rows.applicableStages: All selected stages and views, derived from current project/view/stage identity
rows.requiredEvidence: Actual browser geometry after Save and ordinary navigation at every specified viewport, plus complete operator and restoration replay; no driver scroll inserted before visibility assertions.
rows.observed: The independent regression failed at every tested viewport. After Save, the new Workflow summary was above the viewport while the Project view's previous scroll offset remained active. The existing focus owner intentionally refuses upward forward scrolling. Original raw geometry is retained in the referenced artifact.
rows.interpretation: Different rendered views have different document coordinate spaces. Entering a new project/view/stage initializes that view's scroll coordinate without an animated upward traversal of old content, then the existing forward-focus owner moves down to the destination action. Saved-state restoration overrides neither its recorded view nor scroll. A requirement to preserve globally monotonic numeric scrollY even across replacement of the document's view would conflict with showing shorter destination views without introducing artificial layout space; that alternative reading is recorded for D-4, not silently claimed as proven.
